sentences.text: Briefly stated that facts leading up to the filing of the present petition are as follows:

2.1 On 9th March, 2013, Respondent No. 2 (Complainant) executed an agreement of allotment of unit with the Petitioner company, for purchasing a unit in their proposed project named "Sunshine Business Park" and in lieu of such allotment, paid a total sum of INR 51 Lakhs to the Petitioner company.
2.2 The project could not be completed within the set timelines inter-alia due to change in directorship of the Petitioner company, certain NGT Orders, delay in compliance by Noida Authority etc.

Respondent No. 2 alleged that she was cheated and de-frauded by the Petitioner company and its directors; and as such she lodged the subject FIR No. 264/2019 under Sections 420, 406 and 120B of the IPC against the Petitioner.

2.3 Subsequently, the Petitioner company decided to settle all disputes with the allottees of the uncompleted project by executing a Memorandum of Understanding5,
whereby INR 40 Lakhs was assured to be returned to the allottees - including Respondent No. 2.

Further it was agreed that the remaining balance of INR 20 Lakhs would remain with the Petitioner as an investment and Auction Rate Securities6 and shall be paid to Respondent No. 2 at the rate of 12% per annum on a monthly basis.

In this regard, an unequivocal undertaking was given by the Petitioner to Respondent No. 2 that she can withdraw this INR 20 Lakhs at any time; and if the Petitioner failed to honour this commitment, a ready to move-in apartment in Noida "MoU"

2.4.

Subsequently, a civil suit being CS(Commercial) No. 24 of 2020 was filed by the Respondent No. 2 before the Commercial Court, Karkardooma, New Delhi against the Petitioner company invoking the aforesaid MoU.

The said suit was decreed in favour of Respondent No. 2 and against the Petitioner company, and she was awarded a sum of INR 20 Lakhs along with the agreed upon rate of interest @12% per annum with effect from 1 st April, 2018 till the actual realization of the amount.
Thereafter, Respondent No. 2 also filed an execution petition to realise the decreed amount.

2.5. Now, both parties have settled their disputes and have executed the Settlement Agreement cum Undertaking dated 15th July, 2024, agreeing to settle all their disputes and differences for an amount of INR 26 Lakhs to be paid by the Petitioner to Respondent No. 2.
Further, as per the said Settlement Agreement, Respondent No. 2 has agreed to quashing of the subject FIR.
Respondent No. 2 has also agreed to withdraw her pending Execution Petition subject to payment of the agreed upon amount at the time of quashing of the subject FIR.

3. On 15th April, 2025, the parties recorded their statements before the Joint Registrar of this Court,
confirming the Settlement Agreement dated 15th July, 2024.

5. It is well settled that in the exercise of its inherent powers under Section 582 of BNSS (earlier Section 482 of CrPC), the Court may, in appropriate cases, quash proceedings in respect of non-compoundable offences if the parties have reached a genuine settlement and no overarching public interest is adversely affected.

The Supreme Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab & Anr.7 has held as follows:
"11.

sentences.text: As discussed above, offence punishable under Section 186/332/353 of the IPC are non-compoundable being of serious nature, however, if the Court feels that continuation of criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and justice in this case demands that the dispute between the parties is put to an end and peace is restored, it can order for quashing of the FIR or criminal proceedings as it is the duty of the Court to prevent continuation of unnecessary judicial process.

12. In view of the law discussed above, considering the Settlement arrived at between the parties and the statements of respondent no.1 & 2, I am of the considered opinion that this matter deserves to be given a quietus as continuance of proceedings arising out of the FIR in question would be an an exercise in futility."
2.
[Emphasis added]

6. Further, in Narinder Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab & Anr.,8 the Supreme Court held as follows:
"29.

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid discussion, we sum up and lay down the following principles by which the High Court would be guided in giving adequate treatment to the settlement between the parties and exercising its power under Section 482 of the Code while accepting the settlement and quashing the proceedings or refusing to accept the settlement with direction to continue with the criminal proceedings:
29.1. Power conferred under Section 482 of the Code is to be distinguished from the power which lies in the Court to compound the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
No doubt, under Section 482 of (2012) 10 SCC 303 (2014) 6 SCC 466 This is a Sunshine Tradetower Private Limited vs State Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 8 May, 2025

However, this power is to be exercised sparingly and with caution.

29.2. When the parties have reached the settlement and on that basis petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be to secure:
(i) ends of justice, or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any court.
While exercising the power the High Court is to form an opinion on either of the aforesaid two objectives.
29.3. Such a power is not to be exercised in those prosecutions which involve heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.

Similarly, for the offences alleged to have been committed under special statute like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender.

29.4. On the other hand, those criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.

29.5. While exercising its powers, the High Court is to examine as to whether the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal cases would put the accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal cases."
[Emphasis Supplied]

7. The offence under Section 420 and 406 is compoundable by the person who has been cheated,
while the offence under Section 120B is non- compoundable.

However, it is noted that although the offence under Sections 120B of IPC cannot be treated as strictly 'in personam', and they touch upon public concerns rather than being confined to individual grievances, the Court must also account for the practical realities of securing a conviction in the present case.

In such circumstances, continuing the prosecution may not only prove futile, but would also serve no worthwhile public interest.
The Complainant in the present case has categorically expressed her unwillingness to pursue the matter further and has confirmed the settlement as voluntary and devoid of any coercion.
Given this background, the continuation of criminal proceedings would amount to an empty formality, adding to the burden of the justice system and consuming public resources unnecessarily.

Having regard to the totality of circumstances, and in view of the legal principles laid down by the Supreme Court, this Court finds the present case to be fit for exercise of jurisdiction under Section 528 of BNSS (Section 482 of Cr.P.C.) to secure the ends of justice.

8. In view of the foregoing, the present petition is allowed and FIR No. 264/2019, dated 1st May,
2019, under Sections 420, 406 and 120B of IPC, registered at P.S. New Ashok Nagar, as well as all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, are hereby quashed.
9. It is expected that the parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
10. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
Pending applications, if any, are disposed of as infructuous.
